prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Sugar Land, Texas, and has concussion. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1244; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This call is being recorded for claim purposes. Can you confirm you're comfortable continuing?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Please describe where you were when the collision happened.

A: I was driving on a main road in Sugar Land, heading toward a shopping center. Traffic had slowed down ahead of me because of a light change, so I came to a stop behind a car at the intersection.

Q: What happened next?

A: About a few seconds after I stopped, I felt a hard jolt from behind. My head snapped forward and then back against the headrest. I didn't see the other vehicle coming at all.

Q: Did you exit your vehicle or speak with the other driver at the scene?

A: I got out briefly, but I felt dizzy and had a headache, so I sat back in my car. The other driver came over and apologized. I don't remember everything he said.

Q: Did you seek medical attention?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic that afternoon. They told me I might have a concussion and recommended I rest and avoid screens for a while.

Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?

A: Yes. I still get headaches, especially in the evenings, and I've had trouble concentrating at work. Bright lights bother me more than usual.

Q: Have you been seen by a physician since then?

A: I have a follow-up appointment scheduled with my primary care doctor next week.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything you would like to add to your statement?

A: Only that I want to make sure my medical bills and time off work are covered. I'm still trying to recover, and it's been harder than I expected.

Q: Understood. Thank you for your time today. We will be in touch with next steps.

A: Thank you.
